subject: SKU normalization, entitlement gaps, and billing fallback for AWS Marketplace
messages:
From: Elliot James <procurement@elevatehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@cloudpartners.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood agreement + AWS marketplace activation questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — quick follow-up from procurement: before we sign we need clarity on a few marketplace/entitlement behaviors so our finance ops can map spend to internal cost centers. High-level asks:

1) SKU mapping: our billing system requires a stable SKU per internal product. We noticed multiple marketplace SKUs per product during the PoC. Will Redwood normalize or provide a canonical SKU mapping per tenant?

2) Metering gaps: if a token-ingest failure occurs for a short window (e.g., 10–30 minutes), how do you surface usage and will the marketplace still bill correctly? We need deterministic reconciliation rules.

3) Fallback billing: if your fulfillment webhook fails and AWS retries fail, is there a fallback invoice path? We need an escalation path and SLAs.

Can you put together an ops-level response and the contract appendix we can attach to the SOW?

Appreciate it — Elliot
Procurement Manager, Elevate Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot James <procurement@elevatehealth.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@cloudpartners.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood agreement + AWS marketplace activation questions

Hi Elliot — thanks for the clear list. I pulled ops and legal into thread (cc'd Neha). Below is a concise runbook we can include in the contract appendix; I'll attach the detailed artifacts (SKU matrix, fallback flow diagram, reconciliation checklist) after internal review. Quick answers up front:

1) SKU mapping: Redwood will provide a canonical SKU mapping per product that we maintain as part of the marketplace listing. For customers using multiple pricing tiers we generate an alias map (marketplace SKU -> canonical SKU) and publish it in the activation bundle. We also support a tenant-level override during provisioning for customers that want to map to internal charge codes.

2) Metering gaps & reconciliation: our runtime emits idempotent usage events and stores a local event ledger for 30 days. If we detect missing acknowledged events (AWS reports fewer tokens than our ledger), we:
  - run a reconciliation job (T+1 business day) to compare ledger vs. AWS billing feeds,
  - surface diffs to customer via ledger export and Ticket, and
  - if permitted by contract, submit adjusted usage reports to AWS within the marketplace window (typically 14 days).

3) Fallback billing: we implement a three-step fallback: primary webhook -> queued backoff retry -> invoice backfill. If all retries fail, we produce an SR/Invoice backfill packet that we (a) share with customer finance, (b) push to AWS Marketplace support in parallel, and (c) notify your billing contact. SLA: we commit to initial detection and notification within 2 hours and a remediation plan within 24 hours for production subscribers.

Next steps: Neha, Jordan, and Kim — can you review the attached artifacts and confirm we can provide the canonical SKU matrix and the contract appendix language (I drafted an ops clause). Elliot/Sonia — if this matches your ask I can circulate the appendix and a short statement of work itemized for the activation.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments (to follow): sku_mapping_matrix.csv, proposed-mop-fallback-flow.drawio, elevate_mop_requirements.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot James <procurement@elevatehealth.com>, Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@cloudpartners.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood agreement + AWS marketplace activation questions

Adding a couple of legal/ops constraints that must appear in the appendix:

- Canonical SKU publication: SKU mapping will be included in the activation bundle but Redwood cannot retroactively change marketplace SKUs for historical transactions. We will include a versioned SKU manifest and require a 30-day notice window for SKU renames.

- Reconciliation boundaries: Redwood's reconciliation can propose adjusted usage to AWS; ultimate acceptance by AWS may be subject to AWS Marketplace timing and their support queue. We will include language describing the 'propose and attempt to reconcile' flow and an explicit customer acknowledgement that final vendor-of-record adjustments are subject to AWS acceptance.

- Data retention: our local event ledger retention default is 30 days. For longer retention (90/365 days) we can offer an add-on.

Operational ask for Jordan/Kim: please confirm the sequence IDs in the SKU matrix, and Kim - we need your procurement contact cadence for DocuSign and invoice backfill acceptance.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Elliot James <procurement@elevatehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@cloudpartners.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood agreement + AWS marketplace activation questions

Thanks — that helps. A couple clarifications from our billing team:

- The 30-day ledger default is fine but we need transaction-level exports in CSV (UTC timestamps) and a signed hash for tamper-evidence for any backfill packet. Can you confirm format?

- For SKU renames: the 30-day notice is acceptable if you keep a stable canonical SKU in the contract for our internal chargecodes.

- Fallback invoice backfill: we'll accept queued backfill packets if they contain the signed CSV and your reconciliation delta report. Please include a runbook for how our AR team accepts or disputes backfilled invoices (two-week dispute window).

If you can drop the finalized appendix by Friday (15th) we can get it attached to the SOW and route to finance for signature.

Elliot

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot James <procurement@elevatehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@cloudpartners.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood agreement + AWS marketplace activation questions

Elliot — thanks, we can meet the artifacts and the timing. Deliverables attached and summary below:

Deliverables (attached):
- sku_mapping_matrix.csv — canonical SKU column, marketplace SKU aliases, sequence ID, and tenant override flag.
- proposed-mop-fallback-flow.drawio — visual of webhook -> retry queue -> invoice backfill -> AR dispute flow.
- elevate_mop_requirements.pdf — formatted appendix language ready to insert into SOW (includes 30-day SKU notice, data retention defaults, reconciliation proposal cadence, and SLA commitments).

Format notes: CSV exports will be UTC ISO timestamps, comma-delimited, and include a SHA256 signature file present with each backfill packet. Backfill packet format: signed CSV, reconciliation-delta.pdf, and a Troubleshooting checklist. Dispute window: 14 calendar days from backfill packet delivery.

Action items:
- Marissa: circulate final appendix with DocuSign link by end of day Friday. (I will attach the HubSpot deal link and push to finance).
- Jordan: validate sequence IDs in SKU matrix (ETA EOD Thursday).
- Kim: confirm AR acceptance email address and whether Elevate requires vendor-side PO numbers on backfilled invoices.

Elliot/Sonia — if anything in the appendix needs changing we can iterate quickly; otherwise I'll send DocuSign and a short canary activation checklist so you can validate in your sandbox before go-live.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: sku_mapping_matrix.csv (attachment), proposed-mop-fallback-flow.drawio (attachment), elevate_mop_requirements.pdf (attachment)
